name: Christmas Cactus
hook: Christmas cactus won't bloom? Give it long, cool nights.

steps.title: Bright, filtered light
steps.tip: An east window is ideal. Hot, direct sun turns the stems pale and can burn them.

steps.title: Long, cool autumn nights
steps.tip: From mid-September, give it at least 13 hours of total darkness and 13–18°C nights until buds show.

steps.title: Let the top dry out
steps.tip: Water when the top few cm are dry, then empty the saucer. Standing water rots roots and makes buds drop.

steps.title: Feed through summer
steps.tip: Give half-strength balanced fertilizer monthly while it grows in summer. Stop by the end of September.

steps.title: Pinch tips for more flowers
steps.tip: Flowers form at the stem tips, so pinch off a few segments in spring to make it branch. Root them as cuttings.

outro: Long, cool nights in autumn, then don't move it: blooms follow.

sources.title: University of Minnesota Extension: Growing holiday cacti
RHS: How to grow Christmas cactus

faqs.question: Why does my Christmas cactus drop its buds?
faqs.answer: Usually it's temperature swings, drafts from heaters or vents, moving the plant once buds form, or overwatering. Keep it in one steady spot.
